festivals.name: Island Tourism Festival
festivals.description: A public cultural programme showcases island communities through performances, exhibitions and local food; confirm the organiser’s current schedule.
festivals.story: The Island Tourism Festival is an organised cultural event in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It brings together performances, exhibitions and public entertainment, with visiting mainland troupes joining island-based cultural groups. This makes it different from a single community’s religious festival: its programme is curated by the organisers and can change from one edition to another. The principal urban venue has historically been the ITF Ground in the capital, now named Sri Vijaya Puram. Use the current official announcement to establish dates and venues rather than relying on the festival’s historic January pattern.
rituals: Stage programmes featuring music and dance
Exhibitions and stalls where included in the edition
Participation by island and visiting cultural groups
festivals.food: Food stalls depend on the published programme. Ask vendors about seafood, allergens and vegetarian choices; the event does not have one prescribed festival meal.
festivals.dress: Light everyday clothing and comfortable footwear suit outdoor stalls; performers wear the clothing appropriate to their own traditions.
tips: Confirm the current edition and exact ground before planning travel around the festival.
Treat cultural performances as specific to their participating communities rather than representative of every island community.
places: Capital city reference; verify the ITF Ground entrance and any additional venues.

festivals.name: Rose Festival
festivals.description: Flower displays and cultural activities celebrate the city’s garden heritage.
festivals.story: Chandigarh’s Rose Festival is an organised civic celebration built around the city’s rose gardens and seasonal blooms. It combines horticultural interest with a public festival atmosphere, and the tourism administration usually places it in the late-February period. Visitors can approach it as a garden outing, while any entertainment, competitions or additional attractions depend on that edition’s programme. The Rose Garden is the main geographical reference, but organisers may use surrounding public spaces as well. Confirm the official announcement before assuming a particular activity or opening time.
rituals: Viewing rose displays and garden plantings
Public cultural activities where announced
Horticultural interest and community participation
festivals.food: Refreshments depend on approved stalls and nearby businesses. There is no ritual menu; bring drinking water and ask about ingredients at food counters.
festivals.dress: Comfortable daytime clothing and walking shoes work well. A light layer may be useful for an evening programme.
tips: Stay on permitted paths and leave flowers for everyone to enjoy.
Check the festival’s current programme, access points and transport arrangements rather than relying on a previous year’s listing.

festivals.name: Nariyal Purnima
festivals.description: Fishing communities offer coconuts to the sea, accompanied by prayers and local celebrations.
festivals.story: Nariyal Purnima, also known as Narali Purnima in neighbouring coastal traditions, is associated with coconut offerings and respect for the sea. Daman is one of the places where the festival forms part of local coastal cultural life. Related fishing-community observances express hopes for protection and a fruitful season, while organised cultural activities can add a public element. The ceremonial occasion should not be interpreted as a guarantee of safe sea conditions or a universal date for fishing to resume. Local weather, rules and community arrangements still govern activity on the water.
rituals: Coconut offerings associated with devotion to the sea
Community gatherings in coastal settings
Cultural programmes where locally announced
festivals.food: Coconut features symbolically in the festival. Nearby vendors may offer local snacks; ceremonial offerings should not be taken without guidance.
festivals.dress: Light, respectful clothing and footwear suitable for the waterfront are practical. Community participants may wear festive regional dress.
tips: Confirm the local gathering place with organisers before travelling to the waterfront.
Stay behind waterfront barriers and avoid adding packaging or other litter to the sea.
places: Coastal town reference; verify the designated celebration area.

festivals.name: Diwali
festivals.description: Diyas, family gatherings, sweets and worship mark the festival of lights in the capital.
festivals.story: Diwali, or Deepavali, is a festival of lights celebrated through many regional and community traditions. Lamps, decorated homes, sweets and family gatherings are familiar features, but the stories and ceremonies are not identical everywhere. Worship of Lakshmi is important in many Hindu households, while other communities give the season their own meanings. Public illuminations and markets offer visitors a way to experience the atmosphere without needing access to a private home. Choose a destination and local programme first: the surrounding festive days matter as much as the main night.
rituals: Lighting diyas and decorating homes or public spaces
Family worship and gatherings according to local tradition
Exchanging sweets, greetings and gifts
festivals.food: Mithai and savoury snacks are widely shared; recipes differ across India. Nuts, milk and ghee are common, so ask about ingredients.
festivals.dress: Festive clothing is common. Keep loose fabrics away from oil lamps and choose practical footwear for crowded markets.
tips: Confirm local public events and transport arrangements before choosing a viewing route.
Accept household invitations respectfully and ask before photographing a family’s worship.
places: City reference for markets and public celebrations; choose a specific local programme.

practical.duration: Often observed over five days, with regional differences in the sequence and emphasis.
practical.suggestedVisit: 2–3 days in one city, including the locally observed main evening.
practical.cost: Budget for accommodation, local transport and festive meals. Private dinners, tours and special events have separate prices; no universal visitor ticket is verified.
practical.booking: Confirm the local main evening before reserving accommodation. Ask hosts which celebrations welcome visitors and arrange a return journey in advance.

festivals.name: Eid al-Fitr
festivals.description: Prayers, charitable giving and festive meals mark the end of Ramadan; dates depend on the lunar calendar.
festivals.story: Eid al-Fitr marks the completion of Ramadan, bringing Muslim communities together in prayer, generosity and celebration. Family visits, greetings and shared meals are central to many households, alongside care for people in need. The occasion is observed across India, with distinct local food and cultural traditions rather than a single standard celebration. Its date follows the Islamic calendar and local moon-sighting announcements, so a forecast date should not be presented as confirmed. In Delhi, the neighbourhoods around major mosques can be lively, but worship spaces remain places of prayer.
rituals: Congregational Eid prayer
Charitable giving and support for others
Family visits, greetings and shared festive meals
festivals.food: Sweet vermicelli preparations and other festive foods vary by region and family. Check ingredients and opening times with individual restaurants.
festivals.dress: Worshippers often wear their best or new clothes. Visitors entering a mosque should follow its requirements for modest dress and footwear.
tips: Confirm the locally announced date and visitor access directly with the mosque.
Do not obstruct prayer or photograph worshippers without permission; explore surrounding markets at a suitable time.
places: City reference; confirm access and prayer arrangements at individual mosques.

festivals.name: Herath
festivals.description: The Kashmiri observance of Shivratri centres on family worship, ritual offerings and festive food.
festivals.story: Herath is the Kashmiri Pandit observance of Shivaratri, with a distinctive sequence of household preparations, worship and social visits. The Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts documents the use of ritual vessels and walnuts in the ceremonies, followed by the sharing of soaked walnuts with relatives, friends and neighbours. It is primarily a living family and community tradition, not a single public spectacle. Kashmiri Pandit communities also maintain the celebration beyond the Kashmir Valley, so its cultural geography extends beyond any one destination.
rituals: Household worship involving ritual vessels
Preparation and later sharing of soaked walnuts
Visits and exchanges that renew family and neighbourhood ties
festivals.food: Walnuts have a specific ceremonial role. Other dishes vary by household, and a visitor should ask their host about the meal rather than assume one Shivaratri menu applies everywhere.
festivals.dress: Respectful everyday or festive clothing is suitable when invited. Warm layers are useful for a winter visit to Srinagar.
tips: Join a household observance only by invitation and follow the host’s guidance around sacred vessels.
Confirm any public temple programme separately; it may not reflect the full sequence of home rituals.
places: City reference for Kashmiri Pandit heritage; household ceremonies are private.
sources: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts: Mahasivaratri in Kashmir

festivals.name: Hemis Festival
festivals.description: Masked cham dances and monastery rituals commemorate Guru Padmasambhava.
festivals.story: Hemis Festival honours Guru Padmasambhava at Hemis Monastery in Ladakh. Its cham dances are religious performances, not simply entertainment. The annual dates follow the Tibetan lunar calendar.
rituals: Masked cham dances
Monastery prayers
Ceremonial music
festivals.food: Explore local Ladakhi food outside the ritual spaces; follow monastery rules on eating.
festivals.dress: Modest layers suit monastery visits and changeable mountain conditions.
tips: Ask before photographing religious performances or interiors.
Confirm seating and step-free access with the monastery or organiser.
